reports.title: Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals Reports 2026 Fiscal Year-End Results

desk.headline: Full-year revenue down 46% to $450.8m and loss of $5.11 a share after a $215m review voucher purchase; no financial guidance

numbers.eps_basis: diluted GAAP (full fiscal year; quarterly figures not given in the release)

results: The release covers the full fiscal year only: revenue fell to $450.8m from $829.4m, and the net loss was $724.2m ($5.11 a share).
Costs jumped: R&D rose to $739.1m, SG&A to $202.0m for the REDEMPLO launch, plus a $215m priority review voucher.
Cash and investments rose to $1.19bn, helped by $683.5m of new convertible notes; shareholders' equity fell to $50.3m from $466.1m.
REDEMPLO (FCS) had 950 new-to-brand US prescriptions since launch by quarter end, with new prescriptions up 63% on the prior quarter.
Refinanced its loan into a new $400m facility at SOFR + 5.50% (vs 15% before), maturing 2031; fiscal year-end moves to 31 December.

guidance.summary: No financial guidance. Arrowhead says it is preparing a possible US launch of plozasiran in severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG) in Q2 2027, subject to approval.

points: CEO Christopher Anzalone said the company is moving from scientific promise to a commercial business built around REDEMPLO.
The sHTG filing for plozasiran entered the FDA's STAR pilot, which allows a 6-month priority review; the bought voucher was not needed and is kept.
REDEMPLO is now sold in Germany and approved in the UK, with NHS funding recommended in England and Wales.
Early data on a two-gene drug (ARO-DIMER-PA) and a brain-reaching tau drug (ARO-MAPT) were presented as platform milestones.
The zodasiran Phase 3 study in HoFH is fully enrolled, with completion expected in mid-2027.
call.source: No call coverage found; points from CEO comments and highlights in the press release (8-K Exhibit 99.1)

watch: FDA decision timing on plozasiran in sHTG and a possible Q2 2027 launch.
REDEMPLO prescription growth and first sales figures in the October–December transition period report.
Balance sheet: thin equity after convertible notes and the new $400m loan.
